en: Homage to Śrī Vajrasattva.

By means of the nine types of consecration— which consist of the water, crown, vajra, bell, name, the three families, the pledge (samaya), the worthy master, the secret, and the supreme offering— and which possess immeasurable merit;
I bow to that Tāriṇī, who generates purity of existence. || 1 ||
People, due to their association with the Kali age, have become exceedingly fond of brevity, lacking in effort, and devoid of intelligence.
Therefore, this sequence of consecrations is stated by Vāgīśvarakīrti, omitting the detailed exposition. || 2 ||
Not to a non-Buddhist, not to a fool, nor to one devoted to dry logic;
not to a disciple, nor to a eunuch.
Nor indeed [should one give] to an elder for a child. || 3 ||
These seventh and eighth [mantras] should not be given even to a king, nor to a son, nor to one who lacks faith.
By one who desires the welfare of the Teaching. || 4 ||
[2. Entering the Maṇḍala] [1] First, one who has been duly consecrated therein...

Having been authorized and having mastered the vidyā-mantra through recitation, the mantra-practitioner [should initiate] those seekers who have been prepared by faith, learning, and other such qualities.

Desiring to initiate well-examined disciples through consecrations and other rites, [one should do so] in a mandala-hall or similar location free from all disturbances such as kings and thieves, or within a powder-mandala drawn according to the prescribed ritual.
When the maṇḍala— whether it be one residing on cloth or the like according to the ritual manual,
or one manifested directly as a mental maṇḍala—
is perceived, [one should worship] with flowers, incense, food offerings, and so forth.
Having been honored, and having himself entered by means of the sequence for the entry of disciples preceded by the yoga of his own deity, [he enters] from behind the curtain.
Outside, having given the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā), the disciple who is fit for initiation is visualized in the form of Vairocana;
holding a garland of flowers with the mantra *āḥ khaṃ vīra hūṃ*, his eyes are bound with a blindfold,
and he is sprinkled with water from a flask over which the Vighnāntaka mantra has been recited.
For the purpose of entering the maṇḍala, he should ask:
"Who are you, O lover of delight?
He, in turn, should reply:
"I am fortunate, O Mahāsukha!
thus [he said].
[2] Immediately after that, "Oṃ, I generate the mind of all yoga."
With this, one should generate the thought of awakening (*bodhicitta*).
Then, one should place the vajra together with flowers at the heart with this:
*oṃ surate samayas tvaṃ bhoḥ siddha vajra yathāsukham*.
[3] Then, having entered within the *yamani* by means of the previously mentioned five-syllable mantra, one should speak as follows:

"Today you have entered the family of all the Tathāgatas; therefore, I shall generate in you the vajra-wisdom (*vajrajñāna*). By means of this wisdom, you will attain even the accomplishments (*siddhi*) of all the Tathāgatas, let alone other accomplishments. And you must not speak of this before anyone who has not seen the maṇḍala."
May your agreement not be disturbed.
Thus [it is said].
Then, having placed the vajra upon the head, one should speak thus:
"This vajra shall split your head."
If you should speak of this to anyone: "Oṃ!
Vajrasattva himself is now established within your heart;
he would depart at that very moment, piercing through [your body], if you were to speak of this method. (1)
Having thus caused [the disciple] to take an oath with this, one should recite the mantra *oṃ vajrodaka ṭhaḥ* seven times over water mixed with sandalwood, saffron, and other substances.
This water of hell shall burn you for transgressing the pledge;
through the preservation of the pledge, there is accomplishment. Drink this adamantine nectar-water! (2)
Reciting this, one should cause [the patient] to drink.
Then this should be said:
"From this day forward, I, Vajrapāṇi, am yours."
Whatever I may say, "Do this," that must be performed by you; nor should I be disregarded, lest by failing to avoid danger you bring about your own death and fall into hell.
Thus concludes the drinking of the water of the pledge.
[4] Then, one should effect the descent [of the deity] by means of the procedure for descent prescribed for the mandala and other rites.
[5] Then follows the empowerment through the declaration of truth (*satyādhiṣṭhāna*):
"Thus has this disciple been correctly initiated into the mandala by me; may he possess the lineage of the deities in accordance with his merit. (3) [2a7]
Whatever kind of accomplishment may arise for him, in whatever lineage he is a vessel, and whatever the power of his merit may be—let the mandala be exactly like that. (4)
Having done this,
one should ask: "What kind of appearance does the eye have?"

Then, by means of those [flames] described as appearing white, yellow, red, and black, he should declare, in due order, the suitability for the attainments of pacification (śānti), nourishment (puṣṭi), subjugation (vaśya), and malevolent rites (abhicāruka).
[6] Then, one should cast that taken-up garland into the mandala with this [mantra]: "Accept it, O Vajra! Hoḥ!"
Then, upon the falling of the flower, one should observe the attainment of the inferior, superior, and other levels of accomplishment.

In that regard, if it falls upon the hair-tuft, the crown protuberance, or the head of the Buddhas, there is the accomplishment of the Great Seal (mahāmudrā). If it falls on the eyes or the face, there is the accomplishment of mantra. If it falls on the head, it is the highest [accomplishment].
In the middle part [of the body], it is middling; in the lower part, it is inferior. When far from the *bimba*, success is not immediate; but when near, there is swift accomplishment.

Furthermore, the specific place of each deity should be understood by distinguishing them according to their respective compartments (*koṣṭha*) and so forth. If [the flower] falls between two deities, then that flower belongs to whichever deity it is closer to; that is its family (*kula*).
If [the seed-syllable] falls outside the mandala, a minor accomplishment (kṣudrasiddhi) occurs.

If it falls upon the lines, then one should throw again; even after doing so three times, if it falls in that very same place, there is no success. This is due to falling outside the outer vajra-garland.
There is no accomplishment; however, in the case of a miscarriage, there is a minor result.
Thus concludes the ritual of the casting of flowers.
[7] Then, having taken up that [garland] which was thrown back, he should bind it upon the head of the disciple while reciting:
"Accept this garland, O you of great power!"
[8] Then: Oṃ!
Vajrasattva himself is now intent upon opening your eyes.
The all-seeing Vajra-eye opens up the unsurpassed [vision]. || 5 ||
Reciting thus, he should remove the blindfold.
[9] Then, one should show the mandala for each deity individually, beginning with the gatekeepers and ending with the presiding lord, preceded by the recitation of their names.
Thus concludes the procedure for entering the maṇḍala.
[3. Water Initiation] Then,
just as the great festival was bestowed upon the Buddhas by Bodhivajra, [so it is done here].
For the sake of my protection as well, O Khavajra and others, grant it to me now! || 1 ||
Thus, while contemplating the empowerment for the one who had made this request, [the practitioner] holds the vase and so forth, together with Locanā and the other goddesses:
"The great vajra empowerment, honored by the three realms..."
I bestow [this] which arises from the abode of the three secrets of all the Buddhas. || 2 ||

Having recited this, and having taken water from the vase consecrated by the recitation of the Amṛtakuṇḍalin mantra with the vajra-fist gesture, one should consecrate the disciple like a universal monarch while reciting: "Oṃ vajrābhiṣiñca."
Thus concludes the ritual procedure for the water consecration.

[4. Diadem Initiation] Then, having placed upon the head of the disciple— who is joined with the yoga of his own deity— a crown fashioned from gold, cloth, and so forth, by means of the previously mentioned mantra, one should contemplate all the Tathāgatas residing in the expanse of the sky as being present within the crown in the form of vajras.
Thus concludes the ritual procedure for the crown consecration.
[5. Vajra Initiation] Then, taking up the vajra:
"Today you have been consecrated by the Buddhas through the vajra-consecration."
Take this, which is the state of all Buddhas, as a vajra for the sake of perfect accomplishment. || 1 ||
Reciting thus, and having touched the heart and other parts with the vajra, one should place the vajra in the right hand.
Thus concludes the ritual procedure for the Vajra Empowerment.
[6. Bell Initiation] Then, having had the student perform the gesture of embracing with both hands joined with the vajra and bell held in the left hand,
"Oṃ, I consecrate you as the Vajra Lord; remain, O Vajra, you are the Samaya. Thus one should recite.
The bell consecration itself is called the consecration of sovereignty.
Thus concludes the ritual procedure for the consecration with the bell.
[7. Name Initiation] [1] Thereafter, one should place the vajra and bell upon the head of the disciple: *Oṃ Vajrasattva, I consecrate you with the vajra-name initiation.* [4a][2b6]
One should give names according to the family (kula), such as "O Surata-vajra," "O Suratāṅkura-vajra," and so forth.
[2] (1) By means of these empowerments, one becomes authorized for the hearing and exposition of the mantra-tantras, as well as for the practice of mantra-siddhi.
(2) The five initiations themselves are called the "initiation of the vidyās," because in all cases the vidyās, such as Locanā and the others, are active therein.
Thus ends the ritual procedure for the name-consecration.
8. Irreversible Ācārya Initiation [1] Immediately thereafter, having received the vidyā-abhiṣeka and having undertaken the ācārya-vow, one should say:
"O Treasure of Compassion, grant me the Vajrācārya-abhiṣeka."
May I become capable of accomplishing the welfare of both myself and others through your grace. || 1 ||
Having thus initiated the disciple who has made this request, one should consecrate him with Locanā and the other goddesses through meditative absorption and cause him to undertake the three pledges.
[2] In this regard, this is the threefold commitment:
(1) Having meditated on the vajra with the syllable *hūṃ*:
"The being without beginning or end, Vajrasattva, the Great Joy;
Samantabhadra, the self of all, the Lord of the Vajra-arrogance, the Sovereign."
The Blessed One is the primordial Supreme Person. || 2 ||
Thus, one should cause [the disciple] to grasp the vajra according to its true nature.
Thus is the vajra-samaya.
(2) Immediately after that, [he gives] the bell born from the syllable A.
This is known as the Wisdom of all Buddhas, which follows the sound;
it must indeed always be held by you, for Awakening is considered supreme by the Victors. (3)
With this [mantra], one should place [it] in the hand of the disciple.
For existence is pure by its very nature, yet it is rendered non-existent by [conceptualizing] natures;
through beings who are truly existent and pure by nature, the supreme existence is brought about. (4)
By this [method], the disciple as well should play.
Thus is the commitment of the bell.
(3) Following that: "For the mudrā is declared to be the *samaya* because of the firmness of the mental form; since it makes every form firm, it is therefore proclaimed as 'mudrā'. (5)
By this, one should consecrate the Mahāmudrā, which consists of the form of one's own chosen deity.
Thus is the commitment of the mudrās.
[3] Then, the reality of the mandala, characterized by the purification of the mandala;
the reality of the deity, characterized by the purification of the deity; and the preparation of the preceptor, preceded by the accomplishment of the mandala.
Therein, one should explain these three: the characteristics of the preceptor’s entrance.
[4] Then, having taken as the object of focus the disciple in the form of various deities such as Vairocana and others, one should grant the authorization:
"For the sake of the welfare of all sentient beings, throughout all worlds and in every way, turn the wheel of Dharma everywhere according to the needs of those to be trained. (6)
Thus, with five verses, there is the sequential insertion of the words *dharmasthāni*, *vajra*, *ratna*, *padma*, and *karma*.
Thus ends the granting of permission.
[5] Then:
This is that state of all buddhahood, which resides in the hand of Vajrasattva;
you too must always uphold it, O Vajrapāṇi of firm vows.
With this [verse], one should bestow the vajra.
"Oṃ, O Vajra of all Tathāgatas, remain! This is your samaya; I uphold you, Vajrasattva! Hīḥ Hi Hi Hi Hi Ho Hūṃ.
Thus he addresses the disciple.
One should cause [the disciple] to undertake the vajra-vow.
Thus concludes the bestowing of the Vajra-vow.

[6] Thereafter, having meditated upon oneself as the form of the Buddha, with the left fist at the heart in the gesture of holding the corner of the robe and the right hand in the gesture of granting boons:
Oṃ.
I, the Tathāgata Vajrasattva, prophesy for you, having extracted you from the miserable states of existence, for the sake of ultimate purification from cyclic existence. 8.
Having thus prophesied: "O Tathāgata named so-and-so, you have accomplished the commitment; bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ," [he does so] by means of this Dharma-recollection.
By means of this mudrā, a prophecy is made; he is prophesied for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment with one voice by all the Tathāgatas and by the entire circles of assemblies of noble Bodhisattvas.
This very [mudrā], when invoked...
It should be believed that this is due to the power of Mahāmudrā and the strength of this mantra.
Thus he should speak to the disciples.
Thus ends the exposition.
[7] Then he should speak the secret:
"There is no evil in the three realms equal to dispassion;
therefore, you must never again cultivate detachment from sensual desire. (9)
"Mahāsamaya hana hūṃ phaṭ! Having seen and entered that supreme, most secret, and excellent maṇḍala,
"Completely liberated from all sins, you are well-established this very day. || 10 ||
There is no further death for you from this Great Bliss Vehicle;
your suffering of existence has ceased for the sake of achieving ultimate liberation from cyclic existence. (11)
The bodhicitta must certainly not be abandoned, for it is the seal known as the Vajra.
By the mere production of which one becomes a Buddha indeed; of this there is no doubt. || 12 ||
The true Dharma must never be rejected, nor ever abandoned.
Whether out of ignorance or delusion, he indeed would not reveal it. || 13 ||
The vajra, the bell, and the mudrā must never be abandoned.
The teacher is not to be despised, for he is equal to all the Buddhas. || 14 ||
Having renounced one's own self, one should not afflict oneself with ascetic penances;
happiness should be maintained according to ease, for he is the perfectly awakened one who has not yet come. 15.
Now, you are the master of the mandala, the upholder of the mantra and tantra.
It is esteemed by the Buddhas, the Bodhisattvas, and the deities. || 16 ||
Out of compassion for sentient beings, you should diligently draw the mandala according to the ritual procedure; your own practitioners should be applied to the tantra. (17)
Thus ends the gift of consolation.
[8] And these four, beginning with the permission (anujñā), are bestowed either immediately after the fifth consecration or immediately after the fourth consecration.
The master initiation itself is called the irreversible initiation.

The five initiations and the master initiation [constitute the six]; [the latter] is so called because of the employment of vases in every case. These six initiations are not contradictory even in the Kriyātantra, as they are seen in the *Mañjuśrītantra* and other such texts.
Thus concludes the ritual procedure for the master’s consecration.

Secret Initiation] [1] Then, in a place made secluded by means of a curtain or similar screen, the disciple, having offered to the Guru for the sake of the secret initiation a consort (*prajñā*) who is pleasing to his own mind and endowed with qualities such as beauty of form, and having established her there, should make this request with the words beginning "By the Bodhi-vajra... and so forth.

[2] The Guru, likewise manifesting the three samādhis, having rendered the mind— produced by the lightning-like flash within the lotus of suchness, situated within the vajra-jewel, and personally realized— as non-different from the expanse of space, shall draw it forth from the lotus and release it into the sky of the disciple’s mouth with the ring finger and thumb, beyond the range of the disciple’s gaze.
He too,
saying, "Oh, what bliss! should draw it out and take it away.
One should cause [the mind] to enter into the waves of enjoyment.
[3] Tathatā too, having arisen, while remaining in the midst of her own stainless interior, should—remaining unclothed—playfully place a drop of nectar within the lotus of her face in the sky.
Thus concludes the procedure for the secret initiation of wisdom and means.

[10. Wisdom of Insight Initiation] [1] Immediately thereafter, with the thought that all things are of one suchness (*ekatathatā*), while the disciple—who possesses a different understanding—is in the state of directly realizing self-cognizing gnosis (*svasaṃviditajñāna*) by means of that very [suchness], the master places his own hand upon the disciple’s hand while reciting the previously mentioned verse:
“This delightful *dhāraṇī* of yours is to be cultivated; it has been prescribed by the Buddhas.”
Through the application of the sequence of the wheel, experience true bliss. || 1 ||
Buddhahood and the purification of the three worlds cannot be achieved by any other means;
therefore, never be separated from her.
This is that unsurpassed vidyā-vow of all the Buddhas;
for that fool who transgresses it, there shall be no supreme accomplishment.
Having said this, one should give.

She too, displaying a lotus flower that is smeared with saffron, sandalwood, and other unguents, adorned above with a garland of exceedingly fragrant flowers, and shining forth in its nakedness with extreme clarity, should say this to the disciple:
"O child, are you able to consume feces, urine, and so forth;
blood, semen, and likewise flesh, as well as the supreme devotion to women?"
O child, tell me how you take pleasure in kissing the lotus of her womb.
Thus [it is said].
He replied: "Furthermore, O Queen, I cannot bear the eating of the semen of pimps and the like;
rather, one must always show devotion to women, as well as kissing and [intercourse with] the vulva."
Thus he should say.
[3] Then, she, being delighted,
gazed with affection at the practitioner as if he were her beloved, remaining in a squatting posture like a lotus flower.
Having revealed herself, she should speak thus:
"O, my lotus is endowed with all happiness;
for him who serves it according to the prescribed rite, I stand before him. (6)
O Padmā, perform whatever task is required, such as the propitiation of the Perfectly Awakened One;
for the King of Great Bliss himself is always established right here. (7)
Devote yourself to liberation, Hoḥ!

[4] Having likewise perceived, according to the guru’s instruction, the channel of Vajradhātvīśvarī situated on the left side of the left lotus, while performing the emanation and withdrawal of the array of bees and so forth,
the yogi does not release the *bodhicitta* as long as [the process continues]. [5b]
At that time, one attains something supreme, born of bliss, which is uninterrupted.
But when the bodhicitta, the treasury of all accomplishments, has fallen, and the consciousness of the aggregates has fainted, how can there be any blameless accomplishment? (9)
From the union of the vajra with the element of space and from their contact, there arises a most wonderful bliss which bestows supreme joy. (10)
Between the two joys of cessation (viramānanda), observe the target and make it firm at the place of pressure between the jewel and the central filament within the lotus-space.
While gazing at the mind situated within the jewel from the vajra-paryaṅka posture, whatever gnosis arises—that gnosis is of that very nature; this is sufficient. 12.
Neither passion nor dispassion, nor even the middle way, is perceived;
when the yogi possesses the vision of the Knower, he abides in bliss and does not pass away. 13.
Whether for a watch, or a single day, a fortnight, a month, a year,
or even for a kalpa and a thousand kalpas, he may remain through the application of gnosis.

Having reflected thus and maintained [the practice] according to one's ability, one should release [the seed-syllable] and, having extracted it from the lotus by means of the tongue alone, grasp the *bodhicitta* in the form of the *samaya* with the vision of reality (*tattvadṛṣṭi*).
Thus concludes the ritual procedure for the consecration of the wisdom-knowledge (*prajñājñāna*).
[11. Fourth Initiation] [1] Thereafter, for one who has received the seven initiations and has directly grasped the wisdom of the consort (*prajñājñāna*),
one should bestow the jewel of initiation by means of speech alone.
Through the teacher's instruction, one should impart the form of that which is to be understood.
Thus it has been said:
"Having conferred the initiation according to the prescribed rites, one should examine the disciple's inclination with the mind."
To one who has faith in the vast and profound method, one should indeed bestow the jewel of empowerment with words alone. || 1 ||
Thus [it is said].
Furthermore, for one who has not directly received the initiation of the wisdom-knowledge (*prajñājñāna*),
the initiation by mere word should not be given,
for fear of violating the commitments (*samaya*).
[2] (1) Now, if there is a prohibition against consecration by mere words alone, how then [is it performed] for monks?
Grace should be bestowed [upon others], for they lack the qualification for this [teaching]. Thus it has been said:
"One should not teach the reality (tattva) to those who delight in the state of a monk, nor to those men who delight in logic, nor to those who abide in the state of old age. (Verse 2)
Thus [it is said].
How then is it stated in the *Mahāpratisarā* and other [texts]: "One should visualize the monk as Vajradhara, intent upon threatening the wicked"?
(2) This has already been stated. However,
for that monk who is utterly destitute, a mere ascetic, and whose view belongs to the Śrāvaka vehicle, it simply does not exist.
One possesses authority over mantras, mudrās, and so forth.
However, for that śrāvaka vow which is conjoined with the generation of the Mahāyāna mind, there exists authority regarding mantras, mudrās, and so forth.
(3) But not, however, in the case of the secret initiation and so forth.

However, for that disciple who possesses the vow of a śrāvaka and is endowed with the generation of the mind of awakening (cittotpāda) according to the Mantra method, there is qualification for all [rituals], such as the initiation and so forth. He alone should be appointed as the Vajradhara intent upon the threatening of the wicked.
(4) But even so, how could there not be a violation of the monk's vow?
It would not be so; for thus [it is said]: "By way of non-opposition to the bhikṣu-vow, I receive the vow—external, secret, and belonging to the three vehicles."
By such statements as these, one undertakes additional vows that are not in conflict with other vows.
In that case, how could there be a violation of the vow? Or, let it be granted that one may undertake additional vows that are not in conflict.
(5) But how is there no violation for one who observes the bhikṣu restraint while engaging in the union of the two organs?
Even so, there is no harm.
For it is established that harm occurs to discipline and so forth through the practice of what is prohibited,
but not likewise through the practice of what is not prohibited.
For those who relish passion— characterized by the savoring of tainted attachment toward the beautiful women of gods, humans, and others dwelling within the three realms—
those [women] have been forbidden.
In the Vinaya and other [scriptures],

however, it is not the case that the forms of Mañjuvajra and others— which are the essential natures (svābhāvarūpa) of the deities— are of the nature of mere representation (vijñaptimātra), their bodies being pervaded by the three realms.
Otherwise, there would be a violation of the vow even with respect to those things perceived in dreams that have the nature of objects of conceptual construction.
(6) Furthermore, even regarding those [actions],
for one who rejoices with a defiled mind, thinking, "I have done well; I have done excellently," an offense certainly occurs.

It is indeed true that there is merely an offense, but there is no destruction of the vow (*saṃvara*). However, if one also generates a mind of remorse regarding that [offense], then even that would not be a mere offense. As it has been said:
"Even the most terrible sins committed..."
They become diminished by self-reproach.
Thus it is said.

Thus, even if emission occurs when one acts with passionate haste toward women perceived in a dream or those who are mentally constructed, there is no impairment of the vow (*saṃvara*), nor does it become a mere transgression for one who reproaches himself. Likewise, regarding the Prajñās whose nature is Mañjuvajra and others who have transcended the three realms, and whose own form consists of nothing but one’s own mind— [therein,] the emission is perfectly pure, characterized by non-attachment.

It should be accepted that for those who manifest great passion and then disparage it through the cultivation of the emptiness of its apprehension, there is neither a loss of their status as monks nor merely a formal transgression.

(7) Now, let it be granted that this principle applies to the Prajñā who is of the singular nature of mind alone, whose form is the Svābhā [nature] of Mañjuvajra and so forth; but what of the external Karmamudrā, which is prohibited by the Vinaya?
How is this principle [established]?
It is said:
Have you not even heard here of the proclamation that form and the other [sensory objects] have as their sole essence the mere appearance within one's own mind?
If it is argued that this is stated because it is exactly so,
then those like you have no authority over the Mantra system, which establishes the reality of representation-only (*vijñaptimātra*) or establishes that appearances are merely false forms.
There is [no such thing], because all categories of objects, such as form and so forth, are realized as being nothing but the manifestations of one's own mind.

When the action seal (*karmamudrā*)— which has been transformed into the nature of the consort of Mañjuvajra and others, indistinguishable from the appearance of a woman in a dream, and purified by its illusory-like character— is obtained through faultless consecration, there occurs for monks a violation of their vows (*samvara*).
Thus concludes the ritual procedure for the fourth consecration.

[12. Concluding Verses] This work, which captivates with the luster of a conch shell, the moon, jasmine, the kumuda lily, and the lotus, has been produced by me from the brief words of the *Sekoddeśa*.
By whatever merit [is gained], may the world become equal to the sky,
having the nature of Vajradhara, who is born from the lotus of wisdom.
Thus ends the *Saṃkṣiptābhiṣekavidhi* (The Concise Ritual for Initiation) belonging to the *Sāmājika* [tradition].
This is the work of the great scholar and master, the venerable Vāgīśvarakīrti.
